clue.text: More than just the stomach turning ban on holding the erection flop of 2000

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters are spun round into a new order
holding means one word grips another inside it

blocks.note: the three letters to be rearranged
the Millennium Dome in London, opened for 2000, was a notorious flop

explanation.surface: A stomach-churning tale of banning something that wilted in the year 2000.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'erection' is a building: the Millennium Dome, Britain's much-mocked exhibition structure for the year 2000.
explanation.definitionFit: The abdomen is the belly region containing the stomach plus the intestines and other organs, so more than the stomach.

clue.text: Nerd gets sticky stuff all over female

blocks.note: goo is any sticky substance
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A geek ends up with something sticky smeared over a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'all over' puts the first piece above, so before, the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A goof is a silly or foolish person, a loose synonym for a socially awkward nerd.

clue.text: Loose talk of unemployed wanting energy? Piss off!

indicators.note: something off has gone wrong or is out of place, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: someone idle has no work
go means energy or vigour, as in 'full of go'
the four letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rude rebuff to the work-shy who lack the energy to do anything but chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piss off!' reads as a dismissal; split, the first word is the letters and 'off' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle gossip is careless, unfounded chatter, which is what loose talk means.

clue.text: Long-serving leader's high voice (not a leader of Tories)

indicators.note: not tells the solver to leave the named letters out
'leader of' keeps only the first letter of 'Tories'

blocks.note: a castrato sang with a high voice preserved by castration
taken as written
the opening letter of the party name

explanation.surface: A veteran ruler is mocked for his squeaky voice, unlike any Tory leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': the leader is the high voice minus the A and T that sit side by side in its second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro ruled Cuba for nearly fifty years, one of the longest-serving national leaders.

clue.text: Like many modern parks created by that lot upstairs (not Tony's no.1)

indicators.note: not tells the solver to drop the named letter from what precedes it

blocks.note: them means that group of people
the attic is the room at the top of the stairs
the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: Modern parks, it is suggested, were dreamt up by those upstairs, though not by Tony Blair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That lot upstairs' suggests God or one's bosses; it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Theme parks are built around a single theme, so many modern parks are thematic.

clue.text: Ace body-builder's reported muscles makes you climax

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
surface padding that tells you which muscles are meant: the chest muscles bodybuilders flex
pecs, short for pectorals, are chest muscles

explanation.surface: A top bodybuilder's chest muscles are so impressive they bring you to orgasm.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or peak of something, the same idea as a climax.

clue.text: Pisspoor rapper holding up English bastard — an insubstantial threat, really
Me city centre's abandoned — Conservative cuts?
Gore joins the club with hard messy defeat

blocks.note: gore is spilt blood
a bat is a club for hitting a ball
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Al Gore signs up to a club and suffers a crushing loss.
explanation.walkthrough: Gore reads as Al Gore, the US politician who lost in 2000, but it is just blood.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloodbath is a figurative term for a heavy, one-sided and chaotic defeat, as in an election rout.

clue.text: (see 25dn.)
Belonging to Jeffrey's heart throb eccentric

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle of the name is kept

blocks.note: of expresses belonging, as in 'the house of my father'
the seven-letter name has this letter at its centre
a throb is a pulse or beat

explanation.surface: Something belonging to Jeffrey Archer, novelist and peer, is a strange sort of heartthrob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart throb' reads as one word for a pin-up; split, heart selects a letter and throb is a beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Offbeat describes something unconventional or unusual, a close synonym of eccentric.

clue.text: Overboard type said to make Buddy get tumescent

indicators.note: said tells the solver to go by how the words are spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: Mac is an American way of addressing a buddy, and to swell is to get tumescent

explanation.surface: Someone tossed off a boat is said to excite a friend sexually.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Maxwell, the newspaper tycoon and Private Eye's old enemy, died in 1991 after falling from his yacht.
explanation.definitionFit: The tycoon famously went over the side of his yacht, so the man himself is the overboard type.

clue.text: Goddess at heart, Cherie? Answer: Tony's better half?

definitions.note: Erato is strictly a Muse, a minor goddess

indicators.note: the heart of the name is its centre, so the two middle letters are kept
only half of the name is taken, here its first two letters

blocks.note: the two central letters of the six-letter name
A is the standard abbreviation for answer
the first half of the four-letter name

explanation.surface: Is Cherie Blair a goddess at heart, and Tony's better half?
explanation.walkthrough: Cherie looks like the definition, being Tony Blair's wife, but it only supplies two letters; the answer is the Muse of love poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses, divine daughters of Zeus, who presided over lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: First couple with woman, then bloke and dead woman

blocks.note: Ada is a woman's name
a bloke is a man
D is the abbreviation for dead
Eve is another woman's name

explanation.surface: A tangled love life: a couple, another woman, then a man and a woman now dead.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'woman' comes after 'dead'; the 'and' between them is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Adam and Eve are the first man and woman God created, the original couple.

clue.text: Not in accord with "raging poof test" (university in second position)

indicators.note: something raging is wild and out of control, so these letters are thrown into disorder
this phrase places a letter inside the rest, directly after its opening letter

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A mock-outraged tabloid headline about a test, stated as being at odds with something.
explanation.definitionFit: To be out of step is to disagree or fail to conform, like marching on the wrong foot.

clue.text: Fellow to use tongue on Bowie, say, as a weapon

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
to lick is to run the tongue over
a Bowie is a type of large hunting knife; 'say' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A man licks David Bowie, the rock star, and treats the singer as a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowie reads as the singer, but the Bowie knife is named after the frontiersman Jim Bowie.
explanation.definitionFit: A flick-knife is a knife with a spring-loaded blade, a weapon; Americans call it a switchblade.

clue.text: (& 26ac.) Competition between managers to "incentivise" staff? Being short of a member, you'd have no chance

definitions.text: Competition between managers to "incentivise" staff? Being short of a member, you'd have no chance

blocks.note: surface reading: a corporate scheme to motivate employees; setter's reading: bosses literally booting their workers' backsides

blocks.clueFragment: Being short of a member, you'd have no chance
blocks.note: this completes the saying about a one-legged man, who stands no chance in such an event

explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'as much use as a one-legged man in an arse-kicking contest' is British slang for hopelessness; the member is a leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Managers who motivate by kicking backsides would be in this kind of contest, and the familiar saying names it.

clue.text: Half of long hose gets inverted, look, during bang

indicators.note: something inverted is turned upside down, which in a down clue means read from the bottom
during places one thing within the span of another

blocks.note: to look is to see
a bang is a knock

explanation.surface: A long hosepipe is turned over and bent during an explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: Hose here means stockings, not a pipe; a pair of long socks is the 'long hose', so one sock is half.
explanation.definitionFit: Knee socks are long socks reaching the knee, and one of a pair is half of the hosiery.

clue.text: One pissed off about Tory leader treated like many a NASA launch

definitions.text: treated like many a NASA launch

indicators.note: the leader of a word is whatever comes at its front, its opening letter
about means surrounding, so one word goes round another

blocks.note: a means one
to be pissed off can mean being fed up, or bored
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone fed up with a Tory leader is handled like a cancelled rocket launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' selects the first letter of Tory. 'Pissed off' reads as angry, but here it is fed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Many NASA launches have been aborted, called off before or just after lift-off.

clue.text: Locations of the sleazy dancer's larger notebooks?

blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: a lap dancer performs on customers' laps, so sits on their tops
second meaning: portable computers, bigger than palmtops

explanation.walkthrough: A lap dancer performs on a seated customer's lap; the question mark flags the jokey split of the word into two.
explanation.definitionFit: Laptops are portable computers larger than handheld ones, and split in two the word names the places such a dancer sits.

clue.text: Shame pleb turned into utter shit (in inverted commas), say

indicators.note: turned into says the letters are converted into a different arrangement

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A disgraced commoner is reduced to something worthless, as a tabloid might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: Utter is a verb: to say the word 'shit', quoted, is to swear, as the inverted commas show.
explanation.definitionFit: To blaspheme is to speak profanely or curse, and saying a swear word is an example.

clue.text: He was interested in figures from European Union on vaginal parts (40% circumcised) to date

indicators.note: cutting off forty per cent of a five-letter word removes its last two letters

blocks.note: EU is the abbreviation for the European Union
slang plural for the clitoris
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: A man ogling figures from Europe and a crude anatomical aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figures' suggests bodies; it means geometric shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclid, the ancient Greek mathematician, wrote the Elements, the founding text of geometry, the study of figures.

clue.text: Fate of member squeezed in small car

indicators.note: something squeezed in is pressed inside something else, so one part sits within another

blocks.note: the Ford Ka is a small car
an arm is a member, or limb, of the body

explanation.surface: A cramped passenger asks what happens to an arm crammed into a tiny car.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ford Ka was a small Ford hatchback sold in Britain and Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Karma, in Hindu and Buddhist thought, is the destiny earned by one's actions, so loosely fate.

clue.text: "Composer died during shag!" — Sun
(& 10ac.) No problem getting the 'ayes' to vacillate like vegetables

indicators.note: to vacillate is to waver back and forth, so the letters shift around

blocks.note: the four letters to be rearranged
peas are vegetables, and something pea-like could be called peasy

explanation.surface: A parliamentary whip has no trouble making the yes-voters waver, like a pack of vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: The ayes are those voting yes in the Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy-peasy is a childish British phrase for something very simple, so posing no problem.

clue.text: (see 17ac.)
Parrot house is after city address

blocks.note: EC is the postcode district of the City of London
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A parrot's home is sought in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is after' puts the second piece behind the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat mechanically, just as to echo is to repeat what someone said.

clue.text: For saddos he persists as an anagram of himself

definitions.text: For saddos he persists as an anagram of himself

indicators.note: the clue says outright that one word is a rearrangement of the other

blocks.note: to persist is to live on

explanation.surface: A sneer at fans who insist a dead star is still alive, the name hiding its own claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elvis lives' is the believers' slogan, and the two words share the same five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Die-hard fans insist the King of Rock and Roll never died, so for them he lives on.

clue.text: Boss cat? One to keep a party on the right lines

definitions.text: One to keep a party on the right lines

blocks.note: a chief is a boss
the cat o' nine tails is a whip

explanation.surface: A top cat is described as the one who keeps a political party in line.
explanation.walkthrough: In Parliament the whips enforce party discipline in votes; the chief whip leads them.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief whip makes MPs vote along party lines, so keeps the party on track.
